# Google Workspace Updates: Chat Tables, 1080p Meet Video, and New Flashcards

> **In short:** Google says messages from apps and agents in Google Chat can now include tables and headings, Google Meet on the web sends 1080p video for all users by default, and Gemini Notebook flashcards got three study updates.

You probably have a few tools open all day: a chat window, a video call, maybe a notes app. Google has made small changes to several of them, and most of the changes aim to make information easier to read and easier to keep.

## Tables and headings in Google Chat

Google Chat is where many teams send quick messages. Google says apps and AI agents (programs that can carry out tasks for you, such as gathering information and posting an update) can now send messages with tables and headings.

- **Tables** arrange information in rows and columns. They work well for comparing a few options side by side or tracking the status of several tasks.
- **Headings** split a long message into labeled sections. A summary, a report, or a plan is easier to skim when each part has its own title.

You do not need to do anything to get this. It appears in the messages these apps and agents send you.

## Sharper video in Google Meet

Google says 1080p video, which is Full HD (a sharp picture with about 1,080 rows of pixels, the tiny dots that make up an image), is now available to all Google Meet users on the web. Before this, it was limited to certain paid editions.

It is turned on by default on computers that have a 1080p camera and enough processing power and internet bandwidth (the amount of data your connection can move at once). If your camera or connection is weaker, Meet will not be able to send Full HD, and that is normal.

## Flashcards in Gemini Notebook

Flashcards are small study cards with a question on one side and an answer on the other. Google says it added three updates to flashcards in Gemini Notebook. The company describes them as ways to help you retain information (remember it longer), measure how quickly you recall answers, and keep a steady review routine.

The announcement does not list every detail, so check Google's official post for exact steps before you rely on a specific feature.

## Agent access and admin controls

Google also says its Workspace MCP servers and official Workspace command-line tool (CLI) are now generally available. MCP, short for Model Context Protocol, is a standard way to connect an AI to apps such as email or calendars. A CLI is a text-based tool that lets developers run commands directly. Google pairs these with standardized usage tiers, a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum (an add-on to the terms covering these tools), and expanded controls for organizations to manage AI agents.

## Meeting room touch panels

Starting December 2, 2026, Google says it will reorder the options in the "More actions" panel on Google Meet hardware touch controllers, the tablet-style panels in meeting rooms. The most frequently used actions will move up, so people can reach them with less scrolling.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you join video calls from home, a 1080p camera makes you easier to see, so check that your camera supports it.
- **For your business or work**: Tables and headings can make agent and app updates easier to scan, and the admin controls give organizations more say over how AI agents act.
- **If you're just getting started**: Pay attention to the headings in your work chat. Skimming those first is a quick way to find what matters.
- **If you already use it**: If your team uses agents in Chat, ask them to send status updates as a table so you can compare tasks at a glance.

## Wrap-up

Google's latest Workspace changes are small but practical: clearer chat messages, sharper video for more people, and study tools meant to help you remember things. Pick one of these and try it this week, such as checking your next call's video quality or looking at your next status update in Chat. Then read Google's official post for the full details.
